BiblicalUsage: Sihon is the Amorite king whose land Israel asks to pass through, and who refuses and fights instead. Israel defeats him and takes his cities, from Heshbon to the border, and Moses retells the victory as proof that God fights for His people. The name stands for the first kingdom that falls before Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Sihon matters because he is the first king who learns that refusing God's people is refusing God. The victory at Heshbon is told and retold because it proves the promise is real.
